title: RagResultReady
description: A question was answered, and the answer comes back with what it was built out of. The sources travel so the asker can show its work without holding the chunks. Keys are snake_case, not the camelCase the rest of leaf uses: this travels inside a Liquid envelope, whose own fields (event_id, occurred_at, event_type, owner_unit_ref) are snake_case and pinned byte-exact by signed golden vectors. The shape follows the wire.

session_id.description: The working session the question was asked in.

query.description: The question as asked, repeated so the answer is readable on its own.

answer.description: The answer, grounded in the sources below.

sources.description: The chunks the answer was built from, in order of relevance. Absent when the search found nothing to stand on. A producer of this event always fills in score, chunkType and excerpt, even though the shared shape only insists on the two pointers.

items.title: RagSource
items.description: One chunk the answer stood on. The same shape as common.v1 ragSource, written out here in the relay's snake_case rather than referenced.

asset.description: The asset the chunk came from, as the system that owns the asset names it.

chunk.description: The chunk itself, as the system that owns the chunk names it.

score.description: How close the chunk sat to the question, as the retrieval scored it. Comparable inside one search, not across searches: the scale belongs to the model that searched.

chunk_type.description: Which part of the asset the chunk is — a summary, a transcript, a block of article text. Free text: the vocabulary belongs to whoever chunks.

excerpt.description: The opening of the chunk, carried so a person can see what was cited without fetching it.

asset_title.description: What the parent asset was called when the answer was written. Kept as a copy on purpose: a citation should still read after the asset is retitled.

thumbnail_url.description: A picture of the parent asset, when the system that serves it offers one. Derived, and resolvable only against the deploy that built it.

job_id.description: The job the answer was worked under, when the question arrived as one.
